title: Quantization sensitivity sweep: latency, cost and accuracy trade-offs across FP16/INT8/INT4
creator: Connor Liu
description: Run a focused sensitivity sweep to quantify latency, tokens/sec, p95 and quality impacts for FP16, INT8, and INT4 quantization profiles. Produce a reproducible harness that: (1) exercises steady-state and spike load shapes, (2) measures tokens/sec and p95 including KV-cache warm-up behavior, (3) computes cost-per-1M-tokens estimates, and (4) detects regressions vs baseline using statistical thresholds and effect sizes. Output must include per-layer sensitivity maps and recommended runtime fallback configs.
motivation: We need deterministic guidance for which quantization profiles are safe for production for common Redwood workloads. Previous benchmarks measured throughput but missed p95 and quality regressions exposed only in specific prompt distributions and KV-cache warm-up periods.
success_metrics: Complete sweep across 3 models x 3 quant profiles (FP16/INT8/INT4) for 4 workloads within 12 days
Automated regression detection that flags changes with >95% confidence and Cohen's d > 0.3 for quality metrics
Deliver dashboard with tokens/sec, p95, cost-per-1M-tokens and quality delta for each profile
Provide recommended runtime fallback configs (e.g., dynamic fallback to INT8 on tail latencies)
methodology: Workloads: steady-state conversational, long-context completion (8k), short prompts high-QPS, and synthetic spike bursts
Warm-up: measure first-1k tokens separately to capture KV cache and JIT effects; report steady-state after 10k tokens
Batching: sweep batch sizes [1,4,8,16] and document latency vs throughput curves
Load shaping: run constant QPS, 10x spike for 30s, and 20-min soak test
Quality: automated metrics (perplexity, embedding-cosine vs FP16 baseline) + sampled human eval on 200 prompts per profile
Cost model: estimate infra cost-per-1M-tokens using instance GPU-hour rates and observed tokens/sec
Regression detection: bootstrap confidence intervals, paired tests against current production baseline, and effect-size thresholds (Cohen's d)
workloads_tested: conversational-chat (LLM-chat prompts derived from internal support logs)
metrics_collected: KV cache hit/miss rates and per-request cache-utilization
quality: perplexity delta, embedding cosine similarity to FP16 baseline, human pass-rate
CPU/GPU utilization and kernel occupancy stats
regression_detection: Baseline: FP16 production build (runtime-1.20) with existing batching config
Statistical approach: bootstrap 95% CI for mean difference and use paired Wilcoxon test for non-normal distributions
Effect size: report Cohen's d for quality metrics; require d > 0.3 + p < 0.05 to declare material regression
Latency regressions: flag if p95 increases by >10% and absolute increase > 50ms
Automated alerts: post a Slack thread and create ENG ticket if regression detected across >=2 workloads
False-positive mitigation: require sustained regression across 3 consecutive runs or during a 30-minute soak
implementation_notes: Integrate harness with existing bench runner: add --quant-profile flag and per-layer override file
Instrument runtime to emit per-token timestamps and KV-cache tags for downstream aggregation
Expose per-run metadata: model-version, kernel-set, CUDA/cuDNN versions, and SM arch
Use prometheus pushgateway for real-time collection and export to console dashboards
Add a lightweight human-eval pipeline: random sample of 200 outputs saved to Drive with template for raters
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible benchmark runs produce identical summary JSON within noise bounds
Dashboard populated with tokens/sec, p95, quality-deltas, and cost estimates for all 9 profile combinations
Per-layer sensitivity map identifies top-5 layers where INT4 introduces >0.5 perplexity delta
Regression detector runs in CI and blocks candidate release when criteria are met
Documented recommended profile per workload (e.g., conversational -> INT8+KV-cache warm-up hints)
